newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's OTP, MOL, Pick ineligible for APV payout.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's OTP, MOL, Pick ineligible for APV payout.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt said on Thursday oil company MOL, OTP Bank, and meat processor Pick would not qualify for a payout of privatisation revenues under a 1989 law.

The privatisation law promised state-owned companies which transformed themselved into shareholder companies before 1992 they would receive 20 percent of all subsequent privatisation revenues but APV said it does not apply to banks or to companies which were under direct state control.
"In the transformation according to the privatisation law there are some exceptions, for example state controlled companies and trusts," APV director Csaba Balazs told Reuters.

"OTP was a bank, Pick will not be entitled to the refund because it was under state control, while MOL's predecessor was a trust, the National Oil and Gas Trust OKGT, which also amounts to state control. These are the exceptions."
Two bourse-listed companies have so far received payments under the provisions of the law.

Danubius Hotels Danubius said in a statement on Wednesday that it had received 1.407 billion forints from APV while chemicals firm TVK announced on Friday the agency would pay 4.40 billion forints of privatisation revenues and an additional 842 million of accumulated interest.
Balazs said the 1989 law defined companies eligible for the 20 percent payout as "self-governing" state-owned firms, meaning companies controlled at the time by their employees.
Pharmaceuticals firm Egis and tile maker Zalakeramia are also thought to qualify.

TVK was first to claim the revenues late last year and, following talks with APV, the agency said it had decided to pay outstanding arrears to all eligible companies, amounting to 30 billion forints, by the end of the year.
"All (companies) will be paid at the same time in equal instalments as privatisation revenues come in," APV spokesman Adam Dudits told Reuters at the time.
